data.reason: I act for the service operator under K1, where on_time_deliveries is the main goal and min_company_on_time_rate and unfinished are watched. Option 1's average gain is small and unreliable. On-time moves 271.6 → 273.2 (+1.6), but only 2/5 seeds improve, so in most seeds customers see no gain or a loss. The same change measured −1.2 on 2/5 seeds in period 1, so the evidence across periods points in opposite directions. Unlike D3, where +7.0 justified a 3/5 seed risk, a gain of about 0.6% does not outweigh that inconsistency. The costs are concrete. Road violations rise 20.0 → 21.4, which everyone sharing the roads bears. C's utility falls 69.0 → 67.4, on top of its −12.9 loss in D3. Current service is already strong: lowest on-time rate 0.97, unfinished 0.0, late 3.0. This matches the LLM's recommendation. It departs from the vote result (A ○, B ○, C ×), which would allow adoption. A passing vote permits a change but does not require it, and the vote does not represent customers. Their expected gain here is not shown to be reliable. Keeping v2 has a cost for customers: on average about 1.6 fewer on-time deliveries per period, and the weakest company's customers stay at 0.97 rather than 0.99. Under the current rules they are also not exposed to the losing seeds. The change can return if more evidence shows a consistent gain.
assumptions: The 5-seed measurements are representative of the period-4 busy+rush conditions.
Current v2 performance (on-time 271.6, lowest rate 0.97) will persist under similar demand.
The extra road violations under option 1 would not be offset by safety benefits from less blocking.
unknowns: Whether more seeds would confirm or erase the +1.6 average gain.
Why the same change measured −1.2 in period 1 and +1.6 now.
Whether the added road violations include safety-relevant incidents.
How C's operator will respond to repeated utility losses.
